findings.claim: The public API's response type for txData.chainId changes from number to string; a client that compares chainId to a number or uses it as a number (for example in an EIP-712 domain) will behave differently or fail with no compile-time error, and it is unconfirmed whether safe-wallet web and mobile clients have been updated or are ready to handle the string.
No endpoint-level integration test checks that body.txData.chainId is actually a string; the test only checks that txData is defined, so the new contract on the HTTP response is not locked in.

The invalid-input test cases do not include a missing (undefined) or null chainId, so there is no test guarding against a future loosening of the regex that would let a missing chainId pass (since coercion currently only fails these because "undefined"/"null" don't match the regex).
The regex used to validate chainId accepts strings with leading zeros, such as "01", which would then be passed through to clients unchanged.
